ei.title: Theories and Practices of Sports Fandom
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: Playing sports is one of the most common hobbies, but people also love to watch live sports games. If you go to any sports stadium, you will be able to find fans cheering wildly, crying with joy. In the case of football, some famous matches are accompanied by extreme fans, whose overly aggressive support of their team sometimes leads to confrontations with fans from opposition teams. If someone’s joy, sadness, and even anger emerge from the love of their team, what makes them so loyal? What does it mean for an individual to be a sports fan? And would their passion and cheering actually influence the performance of their team? These questions can be addressed from both an evolutionary and a social psychological perspective. From an evolutionary perspective, sports fandom emerged from our tribal hunter-gatherer ancestors tens of thousands of years ago. At that time, a person was far more likely to survive as a member of a group than as an isolated individual. People could help each other in groups when dealing with difficult tasks, such as carrying hunted animals that were too heavy for one person to handle. This mutual cooperation built trust and fostered relationships among group members. In fact, group membership was so important that tribes with a stronger sense of community were likely to defeat tribes whose members were less closely allied. Because of this, community membership was a survival mechanism for our ancestors, and the instinct to find one’s own tribe or group has been passed down to modern people. This may be how community membership influences our choice of a sports team and our sense of loyalty to that team. There are also two social psychological theories that might explain why we cheer for a sports team: optimal distinctiveness and basking in reflected glory. Though it may be human nature to form a group and feel a sense of belonging to that group, being a fan of a sports team is different from just having friends. Optimal distinctiveness theory states that everyone has a need for inclusion and differentiation. That is, individuals want to be included somewhere, but they also want to be different and unique. These two basic but competing needs can be satisfied through group membership. Sports team supporters are one such group. For example, if you are a fan of a football team based in your city, you can satisfy your need for inclusion by supporting the same team with other in-group members. This can also make you feel unique because your team’s fans are different from the fans of other teams. This feeling of uniqueness is reinforced by sports teams’ deliberate use of their team colors and songs. Another explanation for sports fandom is a phenomenon called “basking in reflected glory.” This means that you feel successful by associating yourself with others’ success, especially when you are connected to them in some way. This phenomenon is closely related to people’s love for their sports teams. People feel proud when their team wins the game or performs well. Even though a team’s triumph may not offer its fans any immediate benefits, the mere act of watching the game brings them satisfaction. This connection with sports teams can sometimes grow so strong among some passionate supporters that they even identify themselves with their teams. Because of this identification, they often consider criticism toward their team as a personal attack and become violent in extreme cases. However, as long as the behavior of sports fans does not go too far and harm others, cheering can become a means for them to express their emotions. Supporting a team passionately can help people forget about their daily life challenges. It can also have positive effects on our brains. For instance, when you cheer for a team and your team wins the game, your brain may release dopamine. Dopamine, a chemical known as the “happy hormone,” makes you feel pleasure when you reach a goal. If you have pursued the goal for a long time, the effect is greater. So it is a particular thrill when a team achieves victory following a series of back-to-back losses. While you are cheering, your brain may also release oxytocin, a hormone that contributes to feelings of bonding between people. Sports fandom brings benefits not only to individual fans but also to the performance of sports teams. When a team competes in their home stadium, their fans gather to watch the game. Typically, the cheers from the home team’s fans are louder than those from the visiting team’s supporters. This dynamic has an impact on the performance of the home team, as confirmed by a study in 2021. The study examined the relationship between cheering and goals scored in matches. It compared home matches in an Italian football league from 2013 to 2019 with matches during the pandemic when crowds were banned from entering stadiums. It was found that the home team’s performance decreased by eight percent on average without crowds. This means that cheering helps the team’s performance to some extent, although it may not be the determining factor. Sports fandom can be analyzed using both evolutionary and social psychological approaches. Through these perspectives, we can understand why people have loyalty and support for their teams. Given that sports fandom has become more and more common in modern times, we should think about our role as fans. We should establish a healthy culture of fandom and seek ways to practice fandom that can have a positive influence on society.

questions.passage: From an evolutionary perspective, sports fandom emerged from our tribal hunter-gatherer ancestors tens of thousands of years ago. At that time, a person was far more likely to (A)[perish / survive] as a member of a group than as an isolated individual. People could help each other in groups when dealing with difficult tasks, such as carrying hunted animals that were too heavy for one person to handle. This mutual cooperation built (B)[trust / conflict] and fostered relationships among group members. In fact, group membership was so important that tribes with a stronger sense of community were likely to (C)[defeat / assist] tribes whose members were less closely allied. Because of this, community membership was a survival mechanism for our ancestors, and the instinct to find one’s own tribe or group has been passed down to modern people.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) 집단의 일원으로 생존 (B) 신뢰를 쌓음 (C) 결속이 약한 부족을 이김
det.analysis:
① survive-trust-defeat: 원문 일치. 집단 안에서 생존(survive)하고, 협력이 신뢰(trust)를 쌓으며, 강한 공동체가 약한 부족을 이긴다(defeat) ←정답
② perish(죽다): '더 잘 생존했다'가 원문이라 반대 ←오답
③ conflict(갈등): '신뢰를 쌓았다'가 원문이라 반대 ←오답
④ assist(돕다): '이겼다'가 원문이라 반대 ←오답

questions.passage: Optimal distinctiveness theory states that everyone has a need for inclusion and differentiation. That is, individuals want to be included somewhere, but they also want to be different and (A)[unique / ordinary]. These two basic but (B)[agreeing / competing] needs can be satisfied through group membership. Sports team supporters are one such group. For example, if you are a fan of a football team based in your city, you can satisfy your need for inclusion by supporting the same team with other in-group members. This can also make you feel unique because your team’s fans are different from the fans of other teams. This feeling of uniqueness is (C)[weakened / reinforced] by sports teams’ deliberate use of their team colors and songs.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) 남과 달라 특별하다고 느낌 (B) 서로 경쟁하는 욕구 (C) 팀 색·응원가로 강화됨
det.analysis:
① ordinary(평범한): 남과 달라 '특별하다(unique)'가 원문이라 반대 ←오답
② unique-competing-reinforced: 세 자리 모두 원문과 일치. 남과 달라 '특별하고(unique)', 소속과 차별화라는 '경쟁하는(competing)' 욕구, 팀 색과 노래로 '강화된다(reinforced)' ←정답
③ agreeing(일치하는): 두 욕구는 '경쟁'한다가 원문이라 반대 ←오답
④ weakened(약화된): '강화된다'가 원문이라 반대 ←오답

For instance, when you cheer for a team and your team wins the game, your brain may release dopamine. Dopamine, a chemical known as the “happy hormone,” makes you feel (B)[pleasure / pain] when you reach a goal. If you have pursued the goal for a long time, the effect is greater. det.korean: (A) 뇌에 긍정적 효과 (B) 목표 달성 시 기쁨 (C) 사람 사이 유대감

② pain(고통): 도파민이 '기쁨(pleasure)'을 준다가 원문이라 반대 ←오답

❌ ④ indifference(무관심) → passion(열정): '그들의 열정과 응원이 팀 성과에 영향을 줄까'가 원문. 무관심은 응원을 이끌 수 없어 정반대 ←정답

② 둘 다 수단: (B)의 This means that은 '의미하다'라 불일치 ←오답
③ (A)수단-(B)의미하다: (A) a means to express = 감정을 표현하는 '수단', (B) This means that = '~을 의미하다' ←정답
④ 둘 다 의미하다: (A)의 a means는 명사 '수단'이라 불일치 ←오답
det.tip: a means (수단, 명사) vs This means that ~ (~을 의미하다, 동사)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
"the quality of being firm and faithful in your support for a person, team, or group"

det.korean: 사람·팀·집단을 향한 굳고 변함없는 지지의 성질 = 충성심(loyalty)
det.analysis:
① jealousy(질투): 정의와 무관 ←오답
② curiosity(호기심): 정의와 무관 ←오답
③ sympathy(동정): 정의와 무관 ←오답
④ loyalty: '충실하고 변함없는 지지'라는 정의와 일치 ←정답
det.tip: loyalty = 충성심, 팀을 향한 변함없는 지지

questions.passage: At that time, a person was far more likely to survive as a member of a group than as an isolated individual. This mutual __________ (cooperate) built trust and fostered relationships among group members.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 흐름에 맞도록 괄호 안에 주어진 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: cooperation: 형용사 mutual의 꾸밈을 받는 명사 자리
det.analysis: 구문 분석: 'This mutual ___ built trust'에서 형용사 mutual(상호의)이 꾸미고 뒤에 동사 built가 오므로 빈칸은 문장의 주어인 명사가 필요하다. 동사 cooperate(협력하다)의 명사형은 cooperation(협력)이다.

questions.passage: Optimal distinctiveness theory states that everyone has a need for inclusion and __________ (differentiate). That is, individuals want to be included somewhere, but they also want to be different and unique.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 흐름에 맞도록 괄호 안에 주어진 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: differentiation: 전치사 for의 목적어이자 inclusion과 병렬인 명사
det.analysis: 구문 분석: 'a need for inclusion and ___'에서 전치사 for 뒤, 명사 inclusion과 and로 나란히 이어지는 자리이므로 같은 명사가 필요하다. 동사 differentiate(구별하다)의 명사형은 differentiation(차별화)이다. 뒤 문장의 different가 의미 단서다.

questions.passage: In fact, group membership was so important that tribes with a stronger sense of community were likely to defeat tribes whose members were less closely allied.  Because of this, community membership was a __________ for our ancestors, and the instinct to find one’s own tribe or group has been passed down to modern people.  This may be how community membership influences our choice of a sports team and our sense of loyalty to that team.  There are also two social psychological theories that might explain why we cheer for a sports team: optimal distinctiveness and basking in reflected glory.  Though it may be human nature to form a group and feel a sense of belonging to that group, being a fan of a sports team is different from just having friends.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 공동체 소속이 조상에게 '생존 장치(survival mechanism)'였다
det.analysis:
① survival mechanism: 원문 'community membership was a survival mechanism for our ancestors'. 소속이 부족의 생존을 좌우했으므로 '생존 장치' ←정답
② social burden(사회적 부담): 소속이 생존을 도왔으므로 부담은 반대 ←오답
③ personal choice(개인적 선택): 본능·생존과 연결되는 흐름과 맞지 않음 ←오답
④ temporary trend(일시적 유행): 조상 대대로 이어졌다는 흐름과 반대 ←오답
det.tip: survival mechanism = 생존 장치, 소속이 곧 생존

questions.passage: This dynamic has an impact on the performance of the home team, as confirmed by a study in 2021.  The study examined the relationship between cheering and goals scored in matches.  It compared home matches in an Italian football league from 2013 to 2019 with matches during the pandemic when crowds were banned from entering stadiums.  It was found that the home team’s performance decreased by eight percent on average without crowds.  This means that cheering helps the team’s performance to some extent, although it may not be __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 응원은 성과를 어느 정도 돕지만 '결정적 요인(the determining factor)'은 아닐 수 있다
det.analysis:
① a complete failure(완전한 실패): 응원이 성과를 돕는다는 흐름과 반대 ←오답
② the determining factor: 원문 'cheering helps the team's performance to some extent, although it may not be the determining factor'. 도움은 되지만 '결정적 요인'까지는 아님 ←정답
③ an unrelated event(무관한 일): 앞에서 도움이 된다고 했으므로 무관하지 않음 ←오답
④ the only cause(유일한 원인): 'to some extent(어느 정도)'라는 단서와 어긋남 ←오답
det.tip: may not be the determining factor = 결정적 요인은 아닐 수 있다
